claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Pack aluminization deposits aluminum onto the surface of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Subsequent heat treatment of the aluminized alloy forms an alumina scale.
The resulting alumina scale will be thin, continuous, adherent, and dense.
The alumina scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Reduced oxygen ingress inhibits rapid oxidation or pesting.
Pack aluminization will markedly improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
Pack aluminization will significantly reduce oxidation or pesting relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Pack aluminization will preserve the alloy's baseline room-temperature tensile ductility.
Pack aluminization will preserve the alloy's baseline yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
The proposed protection is applicable to high-temperature air exposures near 800 °C lasting several hours.
The proposed protection is compatible with tensile-test loading at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Benefits outside the stated temperature, exposure-time, atmosphere, and loading boundaries remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The baseline is explicitly defined as untreated material, but the falsification rule refers to changes relative to a 'treated baseline,' making the intended mechanical-property comparator internally inconsistent.
